text:
maria: Customer reports intermittent SSE sessions dropping after ~20-40s when the client reads slowly (sleep ~150ms between reads). They also see a sharp token billing spike for those sessions. Minimal log snippets attached.

```
[streamer] session=acct-77 stream_id=sn-19 write()=-1 errno=EPIPE
[edge] warn: send() returned EAGAIN, queued=24576 bytes
[proxy] client disconnected mid-body (bytes_sent=768)
```

Repro steps customer gave:
1) Open SSE to /v1/streams/resp with keep-alive
2) Server streams event chunks ~256-1024 bytes
3) Client reads one chunk, sleep 150ms, loop
4) After ~20-40s connection closes and app logs `client write aborted`

Is this straight slow-consumer backpressure (send queue hitting high-water and server aborting), or are we seeing chunk reordering/dup billing due to retries? Any quick mitigations we can ask the customer to apply while we dig in?
thread:
devon: Can you paste full headers from the client + any proxy between them? curious about `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` vs explicit content-length.

maria: they confirmed chunked SSE, proxied through our edge (tls -> edge -> proxy -> streamer). No explicit content-length. headers look standard.

samir: This reads like send buffer saturation + our backpressure policy hitting the abort path instead of pausing. When the kernel returns EAGAIN we queue up to X and then after Y we tear down. Billing spike could be from partial responses being treated as completed tokens on our side if the app closes mid-stream and we didn't mark as aborted in billing pipeline.

ingrid: Quick mitigations for customer: reduce client read sleep (try 30-50ms) to see if the connection stabilizes; or use smaller chunk sizes server-side (eg 128 bytes) so kernel write()s succeed more often. Also ask them to disable intermediate proxy buffering (if any) — some proxies buffer and then burst which amplifies bursts and causes edge queueing. :warning:

samir: Ops-side knobs we can flip short-term: raise per-connection send-queue limit for that customer, and increase socket SND_BUF on the streamer workers. That buys headroom but is just bandaid. We should also ensure aborted streams are labeled `aborted_by_server_backpressure` in billing so it doesn't count as full-completion tokens.

devon: I can push a config change to increase sndbuf for a trial account. @ops-bot can you run `edgectl set-conn-queue --acct acct-77 --limit 65536` on staging and then on prod if stable?

ops-bot: deploy job queued: `edgectl` change for acct-77 on staging (job-id 84321). Will report back in ~5m.

maria: Thanks. Customer is eager for a workaround. I'll propose the 2 client-side tests (lower read-sleep, disable proxy buffering) and offer a short-lived send-queue bump while we investigate durable fixes (adaptive throttling / graceful stall backoff).

samir: Follow-ups for engineering: instrument per-stream queue depth and add a metric that tags streams closed due to write EAGAIN->EPIPE path. We need a billing signal to flag incomplete streams so they don't inflate usage. Also add a server-side small-chunk mode for SSE endpoints.

ingrid: Also hunting if any recent rollout changed `write()` retry thresholds — file a quick blamelist check on the last 48h.

maria: I'll gather client headers, exact proxy type/version, and a packet dump from the customer if they can provide. Keeping thread updated.
